title: What I Learned From Failing
gist_ar: تأمّل شخصي عن التقدم والفشل في تعلّم الإنجليزي.
text:
When I decided to learn English properly, I expected to enjoy it. In fact, I spent the first six months avoiding it.

I kept making the same mistake: I wanted to speak perfectly, so I said nothing. Although I understood the grammar, I avoided every conversation. However, saying nothing is not safe — it is just slow.

The change came because of a small decision. I managed to agree with a colleague that we would speak English for ten minutes every morning, despite how bad it felt. In order to keep going, we made one rule: mistakes were allowed, silence was not.

After three months I noticed that I had stopped translating in my head. My confidence grew, although my grammar was still far from perfect.

My advice is simple. Don't hope to be ready; practise so that you become ready. The goal is not to avoid mistakes. The goal is to make them early, in front of someone kind.

questions.q: What did the writer do for the first six months?
questions.q_ar: الكاتب عمل إيه في أول ست شهور؟

options: Mistakes were allowed, silence was not
They spoke for one hour a day
